name: Spironolactone
route_note: oral tablet or suspension once daily (suspension not interchangeable mg-for-mg)
owner: generic (many); Aldactone brand held by Pfizer

discovery.by: John Cella and Robert Tweit, Searle
discovery.note: A steroidal spirolactone designed to antagonise aldosterone.

tagline: Steroidal aldosterone blocker that cut heart failure deaths in RALES
summary: Spironolactone is a steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist and potassium-sparing diuretic. It reduces mortality in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, treats primary hyperaldosteronism, resistant hypertension and oedema in cirrhosis, and its anti-androgen effects are used off-label in acne and hirsutism.
mechanism: Spironolactone and its active metabolites (canrenone and 7α-thiomethylspironolactone) competitively block aldosterone at mineralocorticoid receptors in the distal nephron, reducing sodium reabsorption and potassium and hydrogen ion excretion.
Blocking aldosterone in the heart and vessels also reduces fibrosis and remodelling, which underlies its survival benefit in heart failure.
It also binds androgen and progesterone receptors, causing gynaecomastia and menstrual changes, and providing the anti-androgen effects used in dermatology.
uses: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (NYHA III–IV)
Oedema in cirrhosis and nephrotic syndrome
Off-label: acne, hirsutism, female-pattern hair loss; feminising hormone therapy

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US as Aldactone.

history.title: RALES
history.detail: Spironolactone reduces mortality by 30% in severe heart failure; the trial stops early.

history.title: Hyperkalaemia warning
history.detail: A population study shows rising hyperkalaemia admissions and deaths after RALES, emphasising monitoring.

history.title: TOPCAT
history.detail: No significant benefit in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction overall, with regional heterogeneity.

history.title: PATHWAY-2
history.detail: Spironolactone is the most effective add-on drug for resistant hypertension.

history.title: Oral suspension
history.detail: CaroSpir oral suspension is approved in the US.

pk.metabolism: Extensive hepatic metabolism to active sulfur-containing metabolites and canrenone

facts: Hyperkalaemia risk is highest with renal impairment and with ACE inhibitors, ARBs or potassium supplements.
Gynaecomastia led to the development of the more selective eplerenone.

references.title: Pitt B et al. The effect of spironolactone on morbidity and mortality in patients with severe heart failure (RALES). N Engl J Med 1999
